correctness.rationale: Stochastic Fubini and the isometry give the target kernel (1−s)^(α+1)/Γ(α+2) and the stated covariance and variance; conditional Gaussian minimization is equivalent to maximizing c(t)^2/(v(t)+η). Its continuous zero limit at t=0 is never optimal. With t=e^x and s=e^y the log integrand is a sum of affine terms and nonnegative multiples of log(1−e^z) at z=y−x and z=y on the convex support y<x≤0. Prékopa applies to the zero extension and gives that u(t)=t c′(t)/c(t) is nonincreasing. After s=tr, the remaining integral has analytic dependence on t on compact interior subintervals (the factor 1−tr is bounded away from zero there), so unequal endpoint slopes force strict decrease. That same scaled integral gives u(0+)=α+1 and u(1−)=2α(α+1)/(2α+1), including α=0. Thus the log-gain derivative H is strictly decreasing, starts positive (1 at η=0 and 2(α+1) for η>0), and its right-end sign yields the stated threshold for α>0 and the unique interior optimum at every finite η for α=0. At equality the gain is still strictly increasing on the open interval. Increasing η raises H at each fixed t; its unique interior root moves right and tends to 1 at activation by continuity. The Brownian quadratic and the α=1 and 2 examples agree with the endpoint calculation; the Brownian root tends to 1 only at infinite noise.
residual_risks: The reported numerical replay is supplementary, not proof or formal verification. This audit applies only to the stated one-site scalar integral objective, normalization and independent absolute noise variance.

value.rationale: In the canonical one-sample Gaussian quadrature problem the result determines when terminal data are exactly optimal at finite noise, not just asymptotically good. It covers all real Volterra orders with a unique maximizing design and explains why the Brownian limit is singular. The concavity argument supplies the global comparison missing from an endpoint derivative calculation alone, and the threshold is directly usable in the specified variance units.
residual_risks: The value judgment is for the all-order classification, not the separately covered α=1 number. No multiple-observation claim is made.
